validator_rule: corpus.py _validate_links semantic pass: verified = {l['source_id'] for l in links if l.get('relation_type') in ('verifies','validates')}; raise if a safety-domain requirement's id is absent from that set.
validator_finding_verbatim: safety requirement has no verifies/validates link
evidence: Validator finding verbatim: 'safety requirement has no verifies/validates link'. Measured against the registry: Link census measured on the registry: verifies links run TMS->FSR (15), TMS->SWR (10), TMS->TSR (7); validates links run TMS->SCO (1), TMS->SGO (1). In the corpus's own convention a test measure is the SOURCE and the requirement is the TARGET, so a well-verified requirement appears as a link TARGET, never as a source. FB2-SAF-FSR-000002 in profile synthetic_reference is the target of at least one TMS->FSR verifies link, but is not the SOURCE of any verifies or validates link, which is what the rule tests. The requirement text is (SOA limit monitoring, debounce 2-in-100 ms, classify within 5 ms), and it is a functional safety requirement with an engineering_domain of safety, so the rule applies to it.
impact: The literal statement 'has no verifies/validates link' is only partly accurate for this artifact. Verification traceability to this requirement demonstrably exists in the corpus, because test measures verify it; what does not exist is a link in the direction the rule inspects. A reader who trusts the finding literally would conclude the requirement is unverified and go looking for missing test evidence that is in fact present. A reader who dismisses the finding as a rule artefact would dismiss it for the security requirements too, where no such link exists in either direction and the conclusion would be wrong.
root_cause: The rule tests only the SOURCE side of a verifies/validates relation, while the corpus's link convention places the test measure at the source and the requirement at the target. Under that convention the rule cannot be satisfied by any requirement that is verified in the corpus's own idiom, so it fires on every safety requirement that has a test. The rule is not wrong to exist - it is the MUT mutation detector for a missing verification link - but its firing on a well-verified requirement is a direction mismatch between the rule and the registry convention, not a traceability defect.
resolution:
RESOLVED. The condition this record detected was real and it was correctly diagnosed in this record's own root_cause: the safety-requirement verification rule in docs/artifacts/tools/corpus.py built its set from the SOURCE endpoint of a verifies/validates link, and under the direction master prompt section 13 declares - 'verifies: verification measure -> requirement/design' - the requirement is the TARGET, so the set could never contain a requirement and the rule reported a gap for every safety requirement including those verified by twenty measures.

WHAT FIXED IT, in two parts, and both were needed. First, the rule itself: docs/artifacts/tools/corpus.py now reads `verified = {l["target_id"] for l in links if l.get("relation_type") in ("verifies", "validates") and l.get("target_id")}`. That correction is recorded as finding FB2-REV-FND-000029 and is not repeated here. Second, and this is the part that was missing from this record's own account: FB2-SAF-FSR-000002 in profile synthetic_reference is the target of 4 verifies link(s) - FB2-LNK-SAF-000014, FB2-LNK-SAF-000022, FB2-LNK-SAF-000043, FB2-LNK-SAF-000050 - from FB2-VER-TMS-000001, FB2-VER-TMS-000008, FB2-VER-TMS-000011. Those links were authored before this record was raised; the rule simply could not see them.

EVIDENCE, re-derived from the live registries on 2026-09-30T00:00:00Z: the rule's population is FB2-SAF-FSR-000002 appears as the target of 4 verifies link(s) and as the source of 0, so the asserted condition 'has no verifies/validates link' is false. The rule is not weakened by the fix and was not weakened here: it is strictly harder to satisfy by accident than before, because a requirement appearing as the SOURCE of a verifies link is a malformed link under the declared direction and no longer counts as verification. Two self-tests pin both directions - 'correctly directed verifies link (requirement as target) not flagged' and 'verifies link with requirement as source does not count as verification'.

RESIDUAL: none for the condition this record asserts. Two limits are stated so that 'resolved' is not read as more than it is. The fix is a link-direction correction, not new verification work: FB2-SAF-FSR-000002 was verified before and is verified now, and this record did not cause that. And a verifies link is a plan, not an outcome - it says a measure exists and points at this requirement, not that the measure was executed and passed. human_approval_status remains pending, production_authorized remains false and product_verification_credit remains false.
